title: First 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle, with Claude
summary: Claude searched protein databases, designed DNA constructs, reduced purification from about three days to about 90 minutes, and processed cryo-EM data into an initial model in 34 hours. The result is a particle made of 96 copies of a bacteriophage protein, with about 25% more internal volume than the mammalian version. Its biological function is unknown; this is a preprint, and Claude made errors that humans corrected.

evidence.tested: The 3D structure was determined by cryo-EM; cryo-EM confirmed the vault shape for four of seven particle-forming proteins, and fifteen altered protein versions were tested, with a reviewer checking the structure.
evidence.unknown: The biological function is unknown, vaults were made only in E. coli, and an unidentified pocket molecule resembling coenzyme A is unconfirmed.
evidence.ai_role: Claude searched protein databases, designed DNA constructs, optimized purification, and ran RELION cryo-EM processing to an initial model in 34 hours; it also made errors that humans corrected.
